title: Getting Along, the Wholesome Way
text: Oh my? Filo-tan (or was it Rafumi?) was threatening Rabbit Guy.
“I hate people who look like usapils!”
“Whoa! Watch out!”
Filo-tan tried to kick Rabbit Guy, but he dodged it.
“Filo, stop.”
“Ehh… no.”
Ignoring Father’s order, Filo-tan attempted a follow-up kick on Rabbit Guy. The monster crest crackled to life, but Filo-tan swiftly suppressed it herself.
“Cut it out. Teo had a reason for laughing.”
Crocodile Guy caught Filo-tan’s kick with his hand and scolded her.
“Ehh…”
“More importantly, ignoring your master’s orders is unacceptable. Do you want to make Shield Hero angry and get thrown away?”
Filo-tan glanced over at Father.
“Nooo. But I hate the usapil person!”
“Hmm… her discipline leaves something to be desired. Shield Hero, you really ought to train her properly, don’t you think?”
Rafumi seized the opportunity to make the suggestion to Father.
“What exactly do you intend to do to Filo-tan!?”
“Discipline her. Don’t you understand, Spear Hero? If left unchecked… my prediction is that Filo will end up becoming a rotten brat just like the traumatized Kou.”
Ugh… she’d end up like a frightened Kou? That absolutely had to be prevented at all costs. But then again, this was coming from Rafumi. Could such words even be trusted?
“Hah… guess there’s no helping it. Filo, if you don’t listen to what I say… you know what happens, right?”
“Ehh…? Noooo!”
Father cautioned Filo-tan with an expression eerily reminiscent of the Father from the very first world.
“I see, I see. So if you absolutely refuse to obey me, I suppose I’ll just have that scary old man over there take you off my hands.”
Ohh… Father pointed toward a monster merchant standing a short distance away as he issued his warning. The merchant grinned wickedly.
“How much would you pay for this one?”

“Well now. She’s a rare specimen, so factoring in the inconvenience fee, I’d be willing to pay twenty gold coins. I’ll carve a heavy-duty monster crest into her—plenty of uses for a thing like that, oh yes.”

Guh… Filo-tan’s face twisted with fear and terror. She had to be protected, no matter what. But the one giving the order was Father himself—and if Father was the one threatening Filo-tan… no! Even if it was Father’s own command, Filo-tan still had to be protected!
“Father, please don’t scold Filo-tan, I say.”
“Motoyasu, you keep quiet.”
Ohh… from the normally gentle Father came a sharp rebuke straight out of the original world. So the act was still very much in progress, it seemed.
“Hmm… this much should be fine. Spear Hero, you’ve earned a few points here.”
Rafumi! What exactly are you calmly analyzing at a time like this!? Filo-tan is terrified! Wasn’t protecting Filo-tan supposed to be the entire point!?
“Spear Hero, you misunderstand something, don’t you? I am a guardian of love.”
“You useless tin can, I say!”
I borrowed a line from Itsuki to level the accusation.
“To be called useless by the likes of you wounds me deeply. Understand this—it was never my role to stop you from pouncing on Filo. Assuming I’m automatically your enemy is a grave mistake.”
While we bickered off to the side, Father wore a wicked grin as he addressed Filo-tan.
“Forced to drink baaad-tasting medicine, poked and prodded all over your body, and in the end… you’ll probably just die, huh?”
“N-noooooo!”
Filo-tan’s anguished scream echoed through the air! I had no more time to waste on the likes of Rafumi.
“Mastaaar, please don’t hate Filo…”
Ohh… Filo-tan clung desperately to Father. Guh… what a heart-wrenching sight this was.
“If you listen properly to what I say, I won’t hate you. So from now on, do as you’re told, alright?”
“O-okay!”
“Then, no more follow-up kicks at that person over there who looks like an usapil.”
“Okaaay.”
Somehow, Filo-tan had managed to obey Father’s order.
“Phew… what a relief. Though if I’d wanted to dodge it, I could have.”
“She really went all out with that kick, huh…”
Filo-tan tilted her head at Father, who answered with such casual familiarity.

“Sorry about that, Filo, really… guess I should explain properly. It was just a side effect of a little act we were putting on—Teo, the usapil-looking guy here, wasn’t laughing at you for any weird reason.”
“Quite right. I certainly wasn’t laughing at your appearance out of genuine mockery. There are plenty of other Filolials in the world, after all.”
“Hmm?”
Filo-tan kept tilting her head, practically radiating a cloud of question marks.
“Having Filo present here complicates matters. My calculation suggests it would be better to have her step away.”
“Yeah, good point… Sadeena-san, would you mind taking Filo… -chan over to where everyone else is? We need to get her some clothes too.”
“Sure thing. Filo-chan, can you drink alcohol, I wonder~?”
“Booo.”
Led away by Older Sister, Filo-tan departed. I trotted along right behind her.
“And where do you think you’re going, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Spear Hero was trying to tag along as if it were the most natural thing in the world.”
“If you follow along here, this whole conversation falls apart.”
“Spear Hero, you’re staying right here.”
Ugh… I’d been called to a halt by Father and the others. No helping it, then—though it pained me deeply to part ways, I had no choice but to join the discussion. Father turned to face Rafumi.
“I understand your goal is making sure Motoyasu-kun and Filo can get along in a healthy, wholesome way, but…”
“Ah, beyond that, I’ll simply entertain him within my own personal discretion as I see fit.”
“That’s… weirdly high and mighty of you.”

Indeed it was. Rafumi puffed out her chest with insufferable pride. Why on earth had a creature like this ended up joining the loop… I’d thought our relationship was confined strictly to that one loop.
“That tail looks just like Big Sister’s.”

“Ah, that’s because my body was designed based on her. A monster was created using fur modeled after the original design, and then I was created in further imitation of that monster. Someone dubbed me the ‘unlovable Raph-species,’ and here I am.”
“That doesn’t sound like much of a boast… and also, ‘Raph-species,’ really…?”
“Is that the only part that concerns you? In any case, I look forward to our continued acquaintance, or some such phrase.”
“So, for now—did it work out okay for Filo-chan?”
“If it hadn’t succeeded, I wouldn’t be standing here. The conditions must have been properly met.”
The experiment had indeed succeeded—but an unnecessary extra existence had sprouted up out of nowhere along with it.
“Ahh… I’d thought I could have both a gentle Father and Filo-tan, but instead an extra nuisance appeared, I say.”
“I feel like I just heard some uniquely awful line specific to loop-users.”
Father remarked with a wry smile.
“So this is the gentle Iwatani-sama? What might the ungentle Iwatani-sama be like, I wonder?”
“The core of it doesn’t change much, but his manner of speech is rougher. Also, his trust in money runs higher. And his aversion to anything sexual in nature is stronger.”
“So even with curiosity present, is the current version—overly reserved as he is—still the better dimension to be in?”
“Shion? Is ‘better’ really the right word to use here?”
Father scolded Crocodile Guy.
“He can be somewhat childish at times, but overall not much different—that’s the consensus among those around him.”

The grumpy Fathers inside my head were lodging their protests. They clearly wished to insist that this was absolutely not the case. But… while it was true he was in a foul mood, it was also true that his underlying gentleness never wavered. That had held true even in the loop where he was reunited with Fleon-chan. When I gifted him a Raph-species, he even added an extra side dish to dinner.
